findings.title: SQL injection via interpolation in migration INSERT
findings.body: The migration interpolates the per-line `h` value from `site_settings.embeddable_hosts` directly into a raw SQL INSERT string: `INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts (host, category_id, created_at, updated_at) VALUES ('#{h}', #{category_id}, ...)`. Any value containing a single quote in the site setting breaks the SQL and any crafted value can inject arbitrary SQL (CREATE FUNCTION, UPDATE site_settings, exfiltration, etc.). The migration must use parameterized queries (e.g. `conn.exec_params(...)` via a PG-specific helper, or sanitize/quote the value) instead of string interpolation. The same applies when `category_id` is 0 and the uncategorized fallback is used as `#{category_id}` — the assumption that this is a safe integer is asserted, not validated, and any non-integer returned by the SQL fallback would also break the query.

findings.title: Migration will fail (or insert garbage) when uncategorized_category_id is the default -1
findings.body: The fallback `category_id = execute(... WHERE name='uncategorized_category_id')[0]['value'].to_i` reads the raw `site_settings.value` for `uncategorized_category_id`. On a fresh install this setting is its YAML default of `-1`, so `category_id` becomes `-1` and the subsequent INSERTs write `category_id = -1`, which either violates the FK to `categories.id` (migration fails partway, leaving a half-applied state) or silently inserts invalid rows that no other code path can legitimately surface. The migration must guard against `category_id <= 0` (no valid category to assign) and either skip inserts or refuse to run with a clear error rather than blindly use whatever integer was read. Additionally, on databases where the `embed_category` lookup returns no rows, `[0]['id']` is `nil` and `[0]['value']` further on can also be `nil`, causing `nil['id']`/`nil['value']` NoMethodErrors that crash the migration.

findings.title: before_validation crashes with NoMethodError when host is nil
findings.body: `before_validation do; self.host.sub!(/^https?:\/\//, ''); self.host.sub!(/\/.*$/, ''); end` invokes `String#sub!` on `self.host` with no nil check. If a record is built without a `host` (e.g. via `EmbeddableHost.new`, the controller's `save_host(EmbeddableHost.new)` flow with no host supplied, or anything that ever constructs a record with `host` unset), Rails calls this `before_validation` callback first and raises `NoMethodError: undefined method `sub!` for nil:NilClass` before the format validation ever runs. Either guard with `self.host = (self.host || '').sub(...)` or move the stripping into a setter / `after_initialize` that tolerates nil.

findings.title: No presence validation on category despite NOT NULL DB constraint
findings.body: The migration declares `category_id` as `null: false` and the controller/admin UI relies on every embeddable host having a category, but `EmbeddableHost` only `validates_format_of :host`. The model has `belongs_to :category` but no corresponding `validates :category, presence: true`. As a result, an admin can save a host via direct API or through any future code path with `category_id: nil` and the failure surfaces only as a generic ActiveRecord `NOT NULL` DB error from the SQL adapter instead of a friendly validation error. Add `validates :category_id, presence: true` (or `validates_presence_of :category`) so the failure mode is consistent with the other validations.

findings.title: update and destroy actions crash with NoMethodError when the host id is invalid
findings.body: `update` does `host = EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first; save_host(host)` and `destroy` does `host = EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first; host.destroy`. If `params[:id]` does not match any record (typo, stale client, manual request), `host` is `nil` and `save_host(nil)` raises `NoMethodError` from `nil.host = ...` / `nil.category_id = ...`, and `nil.destroy` raises `NoMethodError: undefined method 'destroy' for nil`. Both branches should respond with `not_found` (or render_json_error) before calling `save_host`/`destroy`, since the staff user otherwise gets a 500 for what should be a 404.

findings.title: Fabricator file contents appear to be swapped between category_fabricator.rb and embeddable_host_fabricator.rb
findings.body: `spec/fabricators/category_fabricator.rb` after the PR contains only `Fabricator(:embeddable_host)`, while the newly-added `spec/fabricators/embeddable_host_fabricator.rb` contains all of the `Fabricator(:category)` / `:diff_category` / `:happy_category` / `:private_category)` definitions that used to live in `category_fabricator.rb`. The fabricator gem registers by symbol so specs will still execute, but the contents are clearly the wrong way round — the file named for categories defines the embeddable_host fabricator and vice versa — which makes future maintenance (and any code that auto-loads fabricators via filename) confusing and fragile. Move `Fabricator(:embeddable_host)` into `embeddable_host_fabricator.rb` and restore the category fabricators to `category_fabricator.rb`.

findings.title: Migration performs destructive, non-reversible work inside `change`
findings.body: The migration uses `def change` but it does irreversible things inside: it deletes `site_settings` rows for `embeddable_hosts` and `embed_category` and only inserts new `embeddable_hosts` rows. Running `rake db:rollback` will drop the `embeddable_hosts` table (the only part Rails knows how to reverse) but cannot restore the deleted site settings or the host data, so a rollback silently loses configuration. Migrations that move data should be split into explicit `up`/`down` methods, or at minimum copy the affected `site_settings` rows into a backing table before deleting so the data can be restored on rollback. There are also no tests covering the migration's data-move behavior, only the host-validation and host-allow logic.

findings.title: Embedding PUT /admin/customize/embedding is a no-op that silently accepts writes
findings.body: `update` only re-renders `@embedding`; it never persists anything. Combined with the front-end `saveChanges` action in `admin-embedding.js.es6` which calls `this.get('embedding').update({})`, a staff user clicking any future 'save embedding settings' button would appear to succeed (200 + refreshed JSON) while nothing was actually written. If this controller is genuinely a placeholder, it should at minimum 405 / log so it's obvious; if saving per-host records is the intended workflow (which is what the rest of the page does) then the unused `saveChanges` action and PUT route should be removed so future readers don't waste time tracing a dead path.

findings.title: No behavioural specs for EmbeddableHostsController create/update/destroy or save_host
findings.body: The only assertion is that the class inherits from `Admin::AdminController`. The actual behaviour — assignment of `host` and `category_id` from `params[:embeddable_host]`, the fallback to `SiteSetting.uncategorized_category_id` when category_id is blank, the JSON error render when the model is invalid, and the success response shape — has no spec. Given the SQL-injection-adjacent migration and the controller-level nil-handling bug reported elsewhere, this controller deserves at least a happy-path create spec and a 404 / not-found spec.

findings.title: Imported embed posts will fall back to uncategorized when no EmbeddableHost record exists
findings.body: `TopicEmbed.import` now uses `category: eh.try(:category_id)` where `eh = EmbeddableHost.record_for_host(url)`. When the referring host has no matching `embeddable_hosts` row (the previously-existing `SiteSetting.embed_category` was a simple string default), `category_id` will be `nil`, so the post is filed in the uncategorized bucket rather than the admin-configured embed category. Historically a setting ensured there was always a category; with the setting removed, the only path to a real category is registering the host. This is a behaviour change worth flagging for operators who relied on `SiteSetting.embed_category` to retroactively file old imports — it now silently does nothing for unconfigured hosts and any future import race-condition (host not yet saved) goes to uncategorized. Either restore a default-category fallback at the call site or document the new requirement explicitly in `config/locales/server.en.yml`.
